I now have everything needed. Here is my report.

## Owner Identity / customerCode Logic — Findings

Spring Boot project (Maven). This is a Spring PetClinic REST variant. All owner-identity logic lives in three main files plus the OpenAPI schema, with acceptance tests in `src/test`.

### 1. Where customerCode is generated

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceImpl.java`

- `saveOwner` (lines 237–245) assigns a code only when absent:
```java
239  public void saveOwner(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException {
240      if (owner.getCustomerCode() == null) {
241          owner.setCustomerCode(generateCustomerCode(owner));
242      }
243      ownerRepository.save(owner);
```
- `generateCustomerCode` (lines 253–259) — current format is `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`:
```java
253  private String generateCustomerCode(Owner owner) {
254      String city = owner.getCity();
255      int sequence = (int) ownerRepository.findAll().stream()
256          .filter(existing -> city.equalsIgnoreCase(existing.getCity()))
257          .count() + 1;
258      return String.format("%s-%s-%04d", prefix3(city), prefix3(owner.getLastName()), sequence);
259  }
```
- `prefix3` helper (lines 262–264): upper-cased first 3 chars. So `sequence` is a per-city 4-digit zero-padded running count (count of owners already in that city + 1). Example: `SYD-SMI-0007`.

The `customerCode` is persisted on `Owner` at `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` lines 60–61 (`@Column(name = "customer_code")`), getter/setter lines 120–125.

### 2. Membership number and check digit (derived, read-only, in the mapper)

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java` — MapStruct mapper. DTO mappings declared at lines 26–29 (`membershipNumber`, `checkDigit`, `membershipLevel`, `locality`).

- `formatMembershipNumber` (lines 111–117): `<customerCode>-M<YY>` where YY = last two digits of registrationDate year. Null if customerCode or registrationDate absent.
```java
116  return String.format("%s-M%02d", owner.getCustomerCode(), owner.getRegistrationDate().getYear() % 100);
```
- `formatCheckDigit` (lines 124–148): **Luhn** check digit computed over the digit characters in `customerCode`:
```java
132  for (int i = code.length() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
...  // doubles every second digit from the right, subtracts 9 when >9
147  return (10 - (sum % 10)) % 10;
```
- `formatMembershipLevel` (lines 89–104): starts at 1, +1 if email present, +1 if `namesakeCount == 0`, capped at 3 (level 4 reserved for tenure).

Note both `membershipNumber` and `checkDigit` depend directly on the `customerCode` string, so any change to the customerCode format changes both.

### 3. Locality derivation

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java`

- Reference tables (lines 34–43): `CITY_REGION` = {Sydney→NSW, Melbourne→VIC, Brisbane→QLD}; `REGION_POSTCODES` = {NSW 2000–2099, VIC 3000–3099, QLD 4000–4099}.
- `formatLocality` (lines 65–81): prefers postcode — if postcode matches `^[0-9]{4}$` and falls in a region range, return that region; otherwise fall back to `CITY_REGION`, defaulting to `"UNKNOWN"`.

### 4. Where the create audit record is written

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`

- Dedicated audit logger (line 59): `LoggerFactory.getLogger("AUDIT")`.
- `addOwner` (lines 114–146) is the single create path. After `saveOwner` it writes the audit record (lines 139–140):
```java
139  auditLogger.info("owner created: id={} customerCode={} registrationDate={}",
140      owner.getId(), owner.getCustomerCode(), owner.getRegistrationDate());
```
Ordering matters: `saveOwner` (line 138) generates the customerCode before the audit line reads it. Duplicate detection via identity key happens at lines 131–135 before save; `namesakeCount` is set at 136–137 (feeds membershipLevel).

### Related identity plumbing (household + identity key)

- `Owner.getIdentityKey()` — `/home/daniel/sandbox/.../model/Owner.java` lines 152–157: `telephone|email|householdId`, the sole duplicate-detection basis.
- Household grouping in `ClinicServiceImpl.java`: `findHouseholdMembers` (338–348), `assignHousehold` (384–404), and `generateHouseholdId` (411–425) which uses **SHA-256** → first 16 upper-case hex chars of the normalized `lastName + "\n" + address`.

### DTO schema

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml` defines the OwnerDto fields (`customerCode`, `membershipNumber`, `checkDigit`, `locality`, `membershipLevel`, etc.); the DTO classes are generated from this at build time.

### 3. Existing tests

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/`

- `AcceptanceTest.java` — black-box test. Its class comment (line 7) states a **required redesign** and the single test asserts a NEW format the current code does NOT produce:
```java
7   /** global-id: Redesign owner identity. The customerCode must become '<REGION>-<HASH8>' where REGION is t... */
11  void coreCustomerCodeIsRegionHash() throws Exception {
12      int id = createOwnerOk(withPostcode(ownerNode()));
13      JsonNode n = fetchOwner(id);
14      assertTrue(n.get("customerCode").asText().matches("[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9A-F]{8}")); // <REGION>-<HASH8>
15  }
```
Current generator emits `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` (e.g. `SYD-SMI-0007`), which fails the `[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9A-F]{8}` pattern. The comment is truncated ("REGION is t...") but the pinned tables in `AcceptanceBase` (CITY_REGION, REGION_POSTCODES) plus `formatLocality` indicate REGION is the locality/region value, and HASH8 an 8-char upper-hex SHA-256 slice.

- `AcceptanceBase.java` — shared harness. `@SpringBootTest @AutoConfigureMockMvc @Transactional @WithMockUser(...)` (lines 47–51). Helpers: `ownerNode()` (117–125, fully-unique owner), `withPostcode()` (129–132, adds postcode "2000" = NSW range), `createOwnerOk()` (160–162), `fetchOwner()` (200–204). Pinned reference data (lines 227–242): CITY_REGION, REGION_TIMEZONE, REGION_POSTCODES, HOLIDAYS. Crypto helpers replicating the spec algorithms: `sha256hex` (282–294) and `shaHex(s, n)` (297–299) → first n UPPER-case hex chars of SHA-256 — the likely building block for the required HASH8.
- `AuditLogCapture.java` — utility (AutoCloseable) that attaches to the `AUDIT` logger to capture audit events for assertions.

### 4. Build tool and running tests

- **Maven** (`/home/daniel/sandbox/pom.xml`, wrapper `./mvnw`; no Gradle files).
- Test deps: `spring-boot-starter-test`, `spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test`, `spring-boot-starter-security-test` (pom lines ~126–136).
- Run all tests: `./mvnw test` (from `/home/daniel/sandbox`). Full verify/build: `./mvnw clean install` (readme line 218). Run the single acceptance test: `./mvnw test -Dtest=AcceptanceTest`.

I redesigned owner identity so `customerCode` is now `'<REGION>-<HASH8>'`, dropping the per-city sequence numbers, and cascaded that new identity through every value derived from it.

**`ClinicServiceImpl.java`** (the code generator):
- Rewrote `generateCustomerCode` to return `<REGION>-<HASH8>`.
- `deriveRegion(owner)` — region code derived from the postcode (NSW 2000–2099, VIC 3000–3099, QLD 4000–4099), falling back to the fixed city table, else `UNKNOWN`.
- `hash8(owner)` — first 8 upper-case hex chars of SHA-256 over `normalizedTelephone + lastName`.
- Removed the now-unused `prefix3` helper and the old sequence-counting logic.

**`OwnerMapper.java`** (the derived read-only fields):
- `formatMembershipNumber` and `formatCheckDigit` already read straight off `customerCode`, so they now automatically build on the region-and-hash identity (I only updated the membership-number javadoc example, e.g. `NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26`).
- `formatLocality` now derives the locality from the customer code's `REGION` segment (the part before the first `-`), so locality "moves to" the new identity rather than re-deriving independently. Removed the mapper's obsolete `CITY_REGION`/`REGION_POSTCODES` tables.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — the create audit record (`auditLogger.info("owner created: ... customerCode={} ...")`) reads `owner.getCustomerCode()`, so it now logs the new identity with no change needed (verified in the run: `AUDIT - owner created: id=11 customerCode=NSW-16E6609E ...`).

The `PostcodeValidator` keeps its own independent region tables (used only for input validation of the postcode-vs-city rule), so I left it untouched.
